page: Amazon Web Services m6a.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 virtual CPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, providing dedicated CPU allocation. It includes 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, which equates to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor cache configuration consists of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 4 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% with a stress-ng score of 2989.08. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 25% with the same score, reflecting the physical single-core limitation. Memory performance is generally weak, with passmark memory scores and cached small-block read bandwidth falling into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. Real-world tasks show average performance for single-threaded gzip compression and text processing, but poor performance in database operations, software compilation, and redis SET operations, which achieve 2.32 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m6a.large offers a balanced entry-point resource profile for general-purpose workloads that do not require high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-core processing. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-core performance, it is suitable for basic web serving, lightweight text processing, and single-threaded utility tasks. It is less suited for memory-bound databases, complex software compilation, or multi-threaded parallel computing due to its low multi-core scaling and constrained memory bandwidth.
